q: Which two oxides are amphoteric?
explain: Aluminium oxide and zinc oxide are the amphoteric oxides in the syllabus. CuO and CaO are basic and CO₂ and SO₂ are acidic.

q: Which pair of solutions, when mixed, forms a white precipitate?
options: aqueous sodium nitrate and aqueous potassium chloride
aqueous potassium sulfate and aqueous sodium nitrate
aqueous ammonium chloride and aqueous sodium sulfate
aqueous silver nitrate and aqueous sodium chloride
explain: Silver chloride is an insoluble chloride. The other mixtures contain only soluble products.

q: What happens when hydrochloric acid dissolves in water?
options: The molecules are partially dissociated into H⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
The molecules stay intact as HCl molecules.
The molecules react to make H₂ and Cl₂.
The molecules are completely dissociated into H⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
explain: HCl is a strong acid, so every molecule dissociates in aqueous solution.

q: Solid zinc oxide dissolves in both dilute hydrochloric acid and aqueous sodium hydroxide. What does this show?
explain: Reacting with both acid and alkali shows amphoteric behaviour.

q: Aqueous potassium hydroxide and dilute nitric acid are mixed in the correct proportions. Which ionic equation represents the reaction?
explain: K⁺ and NO₃⁻ are spectator ions. Only H⁺ and OH⁻ combine to form water.

q: Which pair of solutions contains the same concentration of acid but a different concentration of hydrogen ions?
explain: A strong acid releases all its H⁺, whereas the weak acid releases only a small fraction, even at the same concentration.

q: Why can sodium chloride not be prepared by adding excess sodium to dilute hydrochloric acid?
options: Sodium does not react with acids.
explain: Sodium is too reactive and would react explosively with the acid. Titration with sodium hydroxide is used instead.

q: Which pair of aqueous solutions does NOT form a precipitate when mixed?
explain: Sodium chloride and potassium nitrate can only form soluble compounds (NaNO₃ and KCl), so no precipitate forms.

q: In the reaction HCl(g) + H₂O(l) → H₃O⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq), which species acts as a base?
explain: Water accepts a proton from HCl to form H₃O⁺, so water is the proton acceptor.

q: Which equation for the reaction of zinc with dilute sulfuric acid is correct?
explain: A metal and an acid form a salt and hydrogen. Zinc forms Zn²⁺, so the salt is ZnSO₄ and the equation is already balanced.

q: Aluminium oxide reacts with both hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide. Which is the correct reason?
options: It is a strong oxidising agent.
explain: Amphoteric oxides react as bases with acids and as acids with alkalis.

q: Blue hydrated copper(II) sulfate crystals are heated strongly. What is the colour change?
explain: Heating removes the water of crystallisation to form white anhydrous copper(II) sulfate.

q: Which oxide is basic?
explain: Oxides of metals are basic. CaO is a metal oxide, but the other three are non-metal oxides, which are acidic.

q: Which row correctly shows the solubility of the salts in water?
explain: Lead(II) sulfate is one of the insoluble sulfates. Nitrates, most chlorides and sulfates of potassium are soluble.

q: Which row classifies the oxides correctly?
explain: CuO and CaO are metal oxides so they are basic, while CO₂ and SO₂ are acidic.

q: Which of these is the best description of an alkali in terms of ions?
options: a substance that produces OH⁻ ions in aqueous solution
a substance that produces H⁺ ions in aqueous solution
a substance that releases electrons in water
a substance that is insoluble in water
explain: Alkalis form hydroxide ions in water. They are soluble bases.

q: Which compound is soluble in water?
explain: All nitrates are soluble. Lead chloride, sulfate and carbonate are insoluble.

q: Which substance is a base but is not an alkali?
explain: Copper(II) oxide is a metal oxide so it is a base, but it is insoluble in water so it does not form an alkaline solution.

q: Which statement about strong and weak acids is correct?
options: A strong acid must be concentrated.
A weak acid does not react with carbonates.
A weak acid can have a high concentration.
A strong acid is partially dissociated.
explain: Strength and concentration are different. Concentration is how much acid is dissolved; strength is how much dissociates.

q: Which statement about nitrates is correct?
options: All nitrates are insoluble in water.
All nitrates are soluble in water.
explain: Every nitrate dissolves in water, so no precipitate forms from a nitrate by itself.

q: Which hydroxide is soluble in water?
explain: Hydroxides are insoluble except sodium, potassium, ammonium and calcium (partially).

q: Excess calcium carbonate is added to dilute nitric acid. Which observation shows the reaction is complete?
options: Bubbles stop and some solid remains.
The solution becomes hot and boils.
explain: CO₂ bubbles stop when all the acid is used, and the leftover solid shows the carbonate is in excess.

q: Which equation shows that ethanoic acid is a weak acid?
explain: The reversible arrow shows that only some molecules dissociate, so ethanoic acid is weak.

q: Copper(II) oxide reacts with dilute sulfuric acid. Which are the products?
explain: An acid and a base form a salt and water: CuO + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂O. No gas is made.

q: Sulfur dioxide, SO₂, is a non-metal oxide. How is it classified?
explain: Non-metal oxides such as SO₂ and CO₂ are acidic oxides because they react with bases and form acidic solutions.

q: Which salts are always soluble?
explain: All salts of sodium, potassium and ammonium are soluble.

q: Which row shows the colours of the indicators correctly?
explain: Methyl orange is red in acid and yellow in alkali. Litmus is red in acid and blue in alkali. Thymolphthalein is colourless in acid and blue in alkali.

q: Which statement about a solution of a weak acid is correct?
options: It contains both undissociated molecules and ions.
It always has a pH above 7.
explain: Only some molecules of a weak acid dissociate, so molecules and ions are both present.

q: Excess zinc is added to dilute hydrochloric acid until no more reacts. Which step is carried out next?
explain: Excess zinc is removed by filtration, leaving zinc chloride solution.

q: Carbon dioxide is bubbled through aqueous sodium hydroxide. What does this show about carbon dioxide?
options: It is a basic oxide because it reacts with a base.
It is a basic oxide because it forms a salt.
It is an acidic oxide because it reacts with acids.
It is an acidic oxide because it reacts with a base.
explain: Acidic oxides react with bases to form a salt (here sodium carbonate) and water.
